steps.what: Observe gauges, recorder and video screens during cardiovascular imaging and recognise abnormal equipment behaviour

tasks.design: Keep continuous observation with the technologist using the imaging-equipment console represented by {OTHER}. No automatic display interpretation or reduction in attention is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Equipment and patient conditions must be understood during the procedure.
tasks.enabler_now: Unrelated image measurement tools do not establish less cardiovascular monitoring effort.
tasks.still_hard: Artifacts and abnormal readings require immediate contextual interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist relates displays to the procedure and patient.
tasks.altitude: No change to monitoring attention or clinical responsibility.

evidence.claim: Live cardiovascular equipment observation remains human work; no validated monitoring-time reduction is established by this digest.

assumptions: Boundary is observing displays during imaging, excluding acquisition setup, diagnosis and reporting.
OTHER denotes the imaging console. Equipment produces its existing readings; no new structured input or machine action is introduced.
No deployment or extra upkeep is proposed, so incremental effort is zero.
research_questions: Which artifacts require direct technologist response during acquisition?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep; live attention is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and distribute diagnostic procedure reports

steps.what: Gather procedure records and verify patient identity, measurements and the technologist's observations
Transcribe and type the procedure report from verified source observations

loop.input: Verified source observations and fixed report headings
loop.check: Technologist checks negation, measurements, units, artifacts and that no diagnosis or observation was invented
loop.stop: One correction attempt; unsupported or ambiguous statements are typed manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text observations require language interpretation; structured measurements use fixed fields

steps.what: Check and distribute the final procedure report to the physician for interpretation

tasks.design: Test native structured reporting in {OTHER}, the clinical records category, before adding bounded dictation-to-draft support in {DOCS}. The technologist verifies the report and recipient before internal distribution; physician interpretation remains separate.
tasks.previous_blocker: Free-text procedure observations need transcription and repeated typing.
tasks.enabler_now: Clinical drafting tools can turn source speech or notes into checked documentation.
tasks.still_hard: Laterality, negation, units and artifacts can change clinical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist verifies what occurred and preserves uncertainty for the physician.
tasks.altitude: Less initial typing; no new diagnostic authority.

reach.learn: Clinical record provenance and correction procedures

evidence.claim: Autoscriber summarises consultations into HiX; this establishes clinical drafting capability, not cardiovascular procedure-report accuracy or this saving.
Applying checked drafting to a procedure report and halving its typing effort is an E1 scenario needing local validation.

assumptions: Boundary is technologist report preparation and internal distribution, excluding procedure performance and physician interpretation; no physician effort is removed.

Technologist produces patient ID, encounter ID, procedure type, acquisition date, verified measurements with units, observations and physician recipient in s1's full 40 hours. Missing or unclear material is manually transcribed in s2, never inferred.
OTHER denotes clinical records and procedure results. Test native report fields first and use only an authorised processing environment; recording is not required.
unknowns: Approved report fields and processing environment
research_questions: Can drafts preserve all measurements, artifacts and negation with less total review-adjusted effort?

incremental.description: Review recurring transcription errors and template changes

approvals.approved_version: Exact report text, measurements, patient encounter and physician recipient; edits void distribution approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=40+20+20=80; gross 20 less 5 upkeep gives net 15. Low is native templates already adequate with no add-on; high requires halved 40-hour typing effort without shorter source or distribution checks.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set up and review ambulatory cardiac monitors

steps.what: Set up Holter or event monitors and explain recording instructions to the patient
Scan and interpret the returned recording, checking rhythm events and artifacts
Report rhythm findings and important recording limitations to the physician

tasks.design: Keep monitor fitting, recording review and reporting with the technologist. Use the existing cardiac-monitor analysis category in {OTHER}; no new interpretation automation is inferred from unrelated EEG tools.
tasks.previous_blocker: Artifacts and patient context need direct recording review.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing analysis aids do not establish a new reduction in technologist time.
tasks.still_hard: Events, diary entries and recording quality require contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist distinguishes artifacts and explains clinically relevant recording limitations.
tasks.altitude: No change in monitor setup, interpretation effort or physician authority.

evidence.claim: The digest does not establish cardiac-monitor interpretation savings; setup, direct review and reporting remain unchanged.

assumptions: Boundary is fitting through reviewed findings and reporting, excluding final physician diagnosis. The separately modelled transcription task is not duplicated here; this report means technical findings and handoff.
Patient produces the recording and diary during existing wear time between s1 and s2, with unchanged effort; no patient-time saving is credited. OTHER denotes cardiac-monitor analysis.
No new deployment or upkeep is introduced; incremental hours are zero.
unknowns: Current monitor-analysis support and review protocol
research_questions: Which recording artifacts consume most direct review time?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 and zero upkeep. Existing acquisition and analysis runtime earns no labour saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule appointments and request clinical supplies

steps.what: Clarify scheduling requirements or supplies needed and capture the administrative request details
Enter verified request details into appointment or supply-request forms
Confirm the appointment with the patient or submit the checked supply request
outputs: confirmed appointment or submitted supply request

tasks.design: Configure native request reuse in {CALENDAR} and {PROCUREMENT} to populate forms from the technologist's verified request. Keep clinical scheduling constraints, patient confirmation, stock assessment and purchasing approval with their existing people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Verified request details are retyped into separate administrative forms.
tasks.enabler_now: Native forms can reuse captured fields without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical urgency, patient availability and suitable supply substitutions require people.
tasks.human_edge: The technologist resolves ambiguous requests and confirms practical suitability.
tasks.altitude: Less form transcription; no new clinical triage or spending authority.

evidence.claim: Native forms can reuse verified appointment or supply details; the duplicate-entry share and savings are E1 scenarios.

assumptions: Boundary covers the technologist's administrative requests; purchasing approval and fulfilment remain outside unchanged. Other workflow is used because appointment and supply activities are alternatives, not sequential dependencies.

Technologist produces request type and, for appointments, patient ID, procedure, duration, permitted date range and constraints; for supplies, item ID, counted stock, requested quantity and cost centre. Capture, stock counting and clarification remain in s1's full 40 hours; clinical staff supply existing ordered procedure and urgency upstream unchanged. Missing fields use manual forms in s3; no free par levels or availability feed is assumed.
Test native forms first. Slot availability is read and chosen by the person in s3, not inferred by the machine.
research_questions: Can verified request reuse cut typing without increasing capture or confirmation time?

already_counted.description: Needs assessment and structured request capture
Patient confirmation, exceptions and checked request submission

incremental.description: Maintain request mappings and inspect failed form population

approvals.approved_version: Exact appointment identity, slot and procedure or supply request items, quantities and cost centre; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=70; gross 30 less 5 upkeep gives net 25. Low is already populated forms with no rollout; high requires 30 hours of observed repeated typing while all contact, stock capture and confirmation remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce report typing and administrative transcription while keeping live monitoring and rhythm review with the technologist.
reach: Help records specialists check procedure provenance
Support patient representatives with practical appointment confirmation
role.ambitious_version: A technologist with less duplicate typing and unchanged attention to patients, equipment and diagnostic recordings.
